ordered_diagnoses: Seizure disorder secondary to cardiac disease

candidates.name: Cerebral Vasospasm
support_spans: clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions
a slight diffuse increase in cortical density predominantly in the right frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
candidates.why: The patient developed seizures and changes in cortical density after cardiac catheterization, suggesting a possible cerebral vasospasm.

candidates.name: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
support_spans: oxygen saturation of 80%
cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage
candidates.why: The patient had a history of complex congenital heart disease, cyanosis, and a cardiorespiratory arrest, which may have led to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

candidates.name: Contrast-Induced Encephalopathy
support_spans: serial doses of nonionic iodinated contrast (Iopromide) totaling 3 mL/kg over 30 minutes
approximately 12 hours after the procedure, the patient developed clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions
candidates.why: The patient received a significant amount of contrast agent during cardiac catheterization, which may have contributed to the development of contrast-induced encephalopathy.
